title: Topic 6.3: Trade and Finance in Islam

pages.lesson:
LESSON: TRADE AND FINANCE IN ISLAM

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.3: Trade and Finance in Islam
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Trade and Finance in Islam, part of Muamalat (Social Relations) in Grade 8 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why are agreements and contracts used in business transactions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. examine the rules on agreements and contracts according to Islamic teachings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. assess the significance of agreements and contracts in Islam,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. practise the rules of agreement and contracts in trade and finance,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate Islamic rules on agreements and contracts.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Trade and Finance in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. examine the rules on agreements and contracts according to Islamic teachings,

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. assess the significance of agreements and contracts in Islam,

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. practise the rules of agreement and contracts in trade and finance,

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate Islamic rules on agreements and contracts.

   Trade and Finance in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the rules on agreements and contracts according to Islamic teachings (Q2:282) in groups and present on charts/PowerPoint,

2. research using digital devices/available reference materials on the significance of agreements and contracts and make notes,

3. dramatise the rules of agreements and contracts,

4. discuss the importance of consumer awareness in relation to making agreements and contracts in groups and present in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the rules on agreements and contracts according to Islamic teachings (Q2:282) in groups and present on charts/PowerPoint,
2. research using digital devices/available reference materials on the significance of agreements and contracts and make notes,
3. dramatise the rules of agreements and contracts,
4. discuss the importance of consumer awareness in relation to making agreements and contracts in groups and present in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Trade and Finance in Islam together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: the skill of experimenting with different ideas enhanced as learners dramatise the

rules of agreements and contracts.

• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology enhanced as learners research on the significance

of agreements and contracts.

• Citizenship: the skill of initiating and entrepreneurship enhanced as learners discuss the rules on agreements and

contracts according to the Islamic teachings (Q2:282) in groups and present in class.

4. appreciate Islamic rules on agreements and contracts.
